findings.defect: The hiccup begins with an erroneous space and lowercase letter.
findings.rationale: The source presents the hiccup as the beginning of the utterance, so standard dialogue capitalization and spacing are required.

findings.current: Miss Song’s eyes had gone half-lidded as she furiously shook her empty glass.
findings.defect: The draft changes unfocused, drunken eyes into partially closed eyelids.
findings.rationale: 눈이 풀리다 describes eyes becoming unfocused or glazed, not the eyelids lowering.
findings.replacement: Miss Song’s eyes had already gone half-glazed as she furiously shook her empty glass.
findings.source: 어느새 반쯤 눈이 풀린 송이 씨가 맹렬하게 빈 잔을 흔들었다.

findings.current: Every now and then, she mumbled incomprehensible things in a slurred voice about how someone had no sense of tact or how rotten luck had latched on.
findings.defect: The draft sanitizes the contemptuous force of 더럽게 and weakens Song’s drunken, aggrieved register.
findings.rationale: 더럽게 intensifies the complaint with coarse irritation, while 재수 옴 붙었다 evokes bad luck sticking like a malign affliction.
findings.replacement: Every now and then, she slurred incomprehensible things about someone having no damn tact and rotten luck clinging like a curse.
findings.source: 가끔은 혀 꼬인 발음으로 눈치도 더럽게 없다느니, 재수 옴 붙었다느니 하는 뜻 모를 소리를 중얼거리기도 했다.

findings.current: Miss Song’s misfortune was soon to become my misfortune.
findings.defect: The draft turns an immediate equation into a future consequence.
findings.rationale: Here 곧 means “namely” or “in turn”: Taekyung treats her present unhappiness as his own rather than predicting that it will affect him later.
findings.replacement: Miss Song’s misfortune was my misfortune.
findings.source: 송이 씨의 불행은 곧 나의 불행.

findings.current: Im Kkeokjeong was egging her on from the side like a bandit who had just found booze.
findings.defect: The draft omits the initial “fish in water” comparison and Taekyung’s comic self-correction.
findings.rationale: The abandoned idiom and immediate revision to a liquor-loving bandit are an explicit humor beat in the source.
findings.replacement: Like a fish in water—no, like a bandit who’d found booze—Im Kkeokjeong egged her on from beside her.
findings.source: 물 만난 고기. 아니, 술 만난 산적처럼 옆에서 거드는 임꺽정은 덤이다.

findings.current: Miss Song was the only person who treated me comfortably.
findings.defect: “Treated me comfortably” is an unnatural calque and obscures that she interacted with him without awkwardness or reserve.
findings.rationale: 편하게 대해 주다 refers to treating someone in an easy, unguarded manner rather than providing them physical comfort.
findings.replacement: Miss Song was the only person who treated me normally.
findings.source: 절 편하게 대해 주는 사람은 송이 씨밖에 없었으니까.

findings.current: “ hic. That was the last one.”
findings.defect: The hiccup again has erroneous leading whitespace and lowercase capitalization.
findings.rationale: The hiccup begins Song’s utterance and should be formatted as such.

findings.defect: The draft makes Taekyung sound as though he is telling Im Kkeokjeong to stop, rather than dismissing the invitation to eat.
findings.rationale: 됐네 here is a curt refusal or dismissal in response to being told to eat, not a command to cease an ongoing action.
findings.source:
“왜? 태경이 너도 빨리 먹어.”

됐네, 이 양반아.

findings.current: If Butler Kim was a has-been, half the mages still active would have to bury their heads in the ground.
findings.defect: “Bury their heads in the ground” is an unnatural English rendering that suggests hiding or denial rather than abjectly lowering their heads.
findings.rationale: 대가리 박다 is a coarse image of putting one’s head down in submission or humiliation; “damn heads” preserves its rough register.
findings.replacement: If Butler Kim was a has-been, half the mages still active today ought to bow their damn heads.
findings.source: 김 집사가 퇴물이면 지금 현역으로 활동하는 마법사 중에 절반은 대가리 박아야 한다.

findings.defect: The Nonsan explanatory footnote is defined but never referenced, leaving an unused Markdown footnote.
findings.rationale: Attaching the existing note at the institution’s first mention fixes the Markdown defect and gives the intended cultural context.

findings.current: “What are you doing? Please, sit down.”
findings.defect: The first sentence is changed into a question about Taekyung’s action and loses Butler Kim’s modest protest that such deference is unnecessary.
findings.rationale: 뭘 또 이렇게까지 gently protests that Taekyung is being excessively formal; it does not ask what he is doing.
findings.replacement: “You don’t have to go that far. Please, sit down.”

findings.current: “Team Leader Choi Minwoo, Team 1, Peace Guild.”
findings.defect: The business-card title is ordered awkwardly and can be read as listing “Team Leader” and “Team 1” separately.
findings.rationale: 1팀장 identifies Choi Minwoo as the leader of Team 1; the replacement expresses that title unambiguously in natural English.
findings.replacement: “Choi Minwoo, Team Leader of Team 1, Peace Guild.”

findings.current: I didn’t know whether Butler Kim was a straw owner or merely a figurehead, but I nodded anyway.
findings.defect: “Straw owner” is nonidiomatic in contemporary US English.
findings.rationale: 바지 사장 denotes a nominal boss with no real authority; “boss in name only” conveys that naturally while preserving the contrast with 얼굴마담.
findings.replacement: I didn’t know whether Butler Kim was a boss in name only or merely a figurehead, but I nodded anyway.
findings.source: 김 집사가 바지 사장인지, 얼굴마담인지는 모르겠지만 일단 고개를 끄덕였다.

summary: The draft is broadly faithful but contains one altered physical description, one temporal meaning error, an omitted joke beat, several register and pragmatic-cue losses, and an unused footnote reference.
